details:
Currently the pelvis is partially clamped to the head orientation when you look too far left or too far right, with this being the ONLY method of hip rotation estimation, this has two problems, one being that you can't look over your shoulder without a hip tracker, and two is that the arms can reach physically impossible angles, breaking immersion, a potential solution I thought of is using the arms to estimate the hip orientation, with the head to assist in cases where that would not suffice on it's own, simular to how boneworks IK does the pelvis, where raising your arms to do a T pose makes the pelvis almost 1:1 orient themselves with your arms, the pelvis would (optimally) still rarely move unless circumstances (calculated based on head and hands) required it.
How'd this behave?
Scenario A: Player is looking forward and moves their hands around, their hip does not move as their hand movements are not moving too far inwards
Scenario B: Player is looking forward, their arms at their sides, they peek over their shoulder, their hip does not move as their arms are still at their sides.
Scenario C: Player moves their left arm way over to their right,  their hip rotates slightly to the right due to the arm angle being physically impossible.
Scenario D: Player turns around, their hip follows as their head and arms are both turning with them.
Scenario E: Player T-Poses, hip rotation is adjusted to the T-pose
title: (3pt) Use controllers to estimate pelvis orientation
